summary: Every piece of content in its own rounded compartment. Tight gaps, varied cell spans, no empty space.
source: Tilda (Bento + cheat sheet + 2025 trends) · UX Planet §28

page.role: the ground the grid sits on

cell.role: one step off the page — never the same value

hairline.role: 1px border, one step lighter than the fill. Load-bearing on dark

accent.role: ONE hue across the whole grid, and it lives in the data

grid.gapNote: the tightness IS the style; 24px+ becomes a card grid

shadow.rule: the hairline border does the separating; heavy shadows are banned

spanVocabulary.rule: a good bento has UNEQUAL cells. A grid of identical cells is a card list, not a bento.

focus.reason: the 1px #2a2a31 hairline is 1.24:1 against the cell fill — far too low to carry a focus state. Focus uses the text colour, which is 15.8:1 on the cell.

motion.note: micro-animations per UX Planet, but nothing decorative inside a cell

copyBudget.headlineReason: cells are small; a headline is a cell label, not a sentence
copyBudget.cellContent: one number, chart or statement per cell
copyBudget.note: TIGHTER than the engine's 420. If your content is paragraphs, bento fights it - use editorial.

a11y.hairlineExemption: The 1px #2a2a31 hairline measures 1.24:1 on the cell fill and does NOT meet 1.4.11. It is legal because a bento cell is a CONTAINER, not a control - 1.4.11 governs UI components and graphical objects needed to identify them. The moment a cell becomes clickable, that border stops being sufficient and the cell needs a real affordance.
a11y.readingOrder: grid span placement can make DOM order differ from visual order. Keep DOM order matching reading order, or place with explicit grid-area.

banned: wide gaps - Tilda: 'very little empty space'
uniform cell sizes - no span variation
heavy shadows - the hairline border replaces them
more than one accent hue across the whole grid
empty filler cells to make the grid resolve

darkMode.note: Bento is dark-FIRST - the sourced specimen is #0d0d0f. Light is the variant, and it is where the hairline nearly disappears: #e4e4e7 on #fafafa is 1.09:1. On light, the border must darken to #d4d4d8 or the cells dissolve.

scroll.headline: scroll-reveal (●), staggered across cells
scroll.reason: cells are flat containers with hairline borders - there is nothing to put behind them

tokenTable: one step lighter than the fill

notes.tokens: Bento is a CSS Grid pattern with a span vocabulary. The design work is deciding which cells span. Four numbers carry it: 4 columns, 74px rows, 10px gap, 18px radius.
notes.nav: A bento nav is a cell like any other — full-width, span 4, same radius and hairline. It does not float and it casts no shadow, because nothing in this pack casts a shadow.
notes.hero: The hero is the 2×2 cell, not a full-bleed band. That is the whole difference from every other pack here: bento has no sections, only cells. Headline ≤6 words because it has to fit a compartment.
notes.button: The only place an accent is allowed to touch a container. Focus is a 2px #f5f5f7 ring at 2px offset — not the hairline, which measures 1.24:1 against the cell and cannot carry a state.
notes.form: An input is a cell with a darker fill. The error state cannot use a red border alone (colour-only signalling, WCAG 1.4.1) and cannot use a heavy shadow, so it uses a filled label row inside the cell.
notes.card: In bento the card is the cell. There is no separate card component — which is why span variation carries all the hierarchy. A grid of identical cells is a card list, not a bento.
notes.table: Bento's weakest module. A table wants rules and alignment; a cell wants a single summarisable value. When the content is genuinely tabular, give the table one full-width span 4 cell and let it be a table inside it.
notes.overlay: No blur — backdrop-filter is glassmorphism's vocabulary. The scrim is flat rgba(0,0,0,.72) and the dialog is simply a cell that happens to be centred.
notes.empty: An empty cell is the one thing this pack bans outright — Tilda: no empty filler cells to make the grid resolve. So an empty state is a cell with a dashed hairline that states what is missing, never a blank compartment.
notes.dark: Bento is dark-first: the sourced specimen is #0d0d0f. Light is the variant, and it is where the pack breaks — #e4e4e7 on #fafafa is 1.09:1 and the cells dissolve. On light the hairline must darken to #d4d4d8.
notes.narrow: This is where bento breaks, and its own gotchas say so. Four columns collapsing to one turns a considered composition into a stack of boxes, and the 2×2 hero becomes a tall empty rectangle. Change grid-row: span at breakpoints — do not just let it reflow.
notes.copy: Each cell needs a single number, chart or statement. charsPerViewport is 300, well under the engine's 420, because the container is a compartment.
